--- title: iOS description: Run Rust and TSX NSH apps on iOS with UIKit views, in the simulator or on devices, package them as .app and .ipa, and embed them in an existing iOS app with AppView or NativeShell.xcframework's NshAppView. order: 11 group: platforms --- # iOS NSH apps run on iOS with UIKit views and CoreText text, on devices and in the simulator, from iOS 15.0. Whole apps run and package as on the other platforms, and an existing app can show NSH apps in its own views, a Rust root it links or TSX it loads, including signed packages it downloads, under limits and capabilities it sets. On iOS, `os()` is `Os::Ios` (`platform.os` is `"ios"` in TSX) and TSX's `ios={{…}}` props apply. ## Requirements - **Xcode** on a Mac, with an iOS simulator runtime (`xcodebuild -downloadPlatform iOS` installs one). See [Installation](./installation.md#ios-and-mac-catalyst). - Apps need **iOS 15.0** or later, on iPhone and iPad. ## Running an app A Rust app runs from its directory, a TSX app names its entry: ```sh nsh run --target ios # a Rust app nsh run --target ios --device "iPhone 16 Pro" nsh run App.tsx --target ios # a TSX app ``` `nsh` uses a booted simulator, or boots the newest iPhone. For a Rust app it builds the app's own runner with your crate, installs it and shows its logs in the terminal; a change to the crate's Rust code builds it again and restarts the app. For a TSX app it installs the development host and keeps the app up to date as you save, with logs in the terminal. `--device` picks a simulator by name or UDID. For a quicker loop without a simulator, `nsh run --target catalyst` on a Mac opens the same UIKit backend in an iPhone-sized [Mac Catalyst](./getting-started.md#mac-catalyst) window. ## Packaging ```sh nsh package --target ios-simulator --run # .nsh/out/.app, installed and launched in the simulator nsh package --target ios --sign "Apple Distribution: Example Inc (ABCDE12345)" --profile AppStore.mobileprovision ``` From a Rust app's directory, the app is the iOS runner built with your crate; a TSX app names its entry (`nsh package App.tsx --target ios-simulator --run`). `--target ios` writes a signed `.ipa` for devices, TestFlight or the App Store. Signing identities, provisioning profiles and icons: [Packaging](./packaging.md#ios-devices). ## Embedding in an iOS app An existing iOS app can show NSH apps inside its own UI. An iOS app with Rust code links your crate and the `nsh-platform-ios` crate and shows your root in an `AppView` ([Embedding a Rust app](#embedding-a-rust-app)). A Swift app links `NativeShell.xcframework`, a framework with a Swift module: you create an `NshAppView` (a `UIView`), add it anywhere in your view hierarchy and load a TSX app or a signed package into it. Your native screens, navigation and the NSH app live side by side in one UIKit hierarchy. Each view is one independent engine; there are no global singletons, so an app can show several NSH apps at once, for example one per tab.
## Embedding a Rust app `nsh_platform_ios::AppView` is one engine as a `UIView` for an iOS app built with Rust: it mounts your crate's root component, with no JavaScript VM involved. ```rust use nsh_platform_ios::{set_ui_sets, AppView, Root, SurfaceOptions}; use objc2::MainThreadMarker; use objc2_ui_kit::UIView; fn show(container: &UIView) -> AppView { // Once, before the first view: the UI sets the apps import (NSH's and your crate's). set_ui_sets(vec![nsh_base::registry(), my_app::registry()]); let mtm = MainThreadMarker::new().expect("main thread"); let app = AppView::new(mtm, container.bounds(), SurfaceOptions::default()); container.addSubview(app.view()); app.run(Root::of::()); // Keep the AppView: dropping it stops the app. app } ``` The view resizes with its superview. `AppView::run` replaces whatever ran; `AppView::load` runs a TSX bundle instead (`Bundle::source`, or `unsafe { Bundle::bytecode(bytes) }` for a `bundle.nshc` in the app bundle). `SurfaceOptions` holds the limits, the granted capabilities, the data directory and the native components, as `NshAppView`'s members below do; `AppView::set_locale`, `set_font_scale` and `set_error_handler` match `locale`, `fontScale` and `onError`. `nsh package --target ios` builds this kind of app for you, with your root mounted. ## Get the framework The distribution contains both variants: ```text dist/nsh/embed/ios/NativeShell.xcframework release: bundles and signed packages dist/nsh/embed/ios/NativeShellDev.xcframework also connects to a `nsh dev` server ``` From a checkout of NSH you can build just the frameworks: ```sh cargo xtask ios-embed # writes dist/nsh/embed/ios/{NativeShell,NativeShellDev}.xcframework ``` The default build produces static frameworks. To build dynamic frameworks, use: ```sh cargo xtask ios-embed --dynamic ``` Dynamic frameworks give the runtime its own library image and unwind table, supporting host apps that already link other Rust runtimes. Choose the Xcode embedding setting below to match the framework you build. By default, each XCFramework has three arm64 slices: iOS devices, the iOS simulator (Apple silicon) and Mac Catalyst. The minimum deployment target is iOS 15.0. The Swift module is compiled with library evolution, so apps built with other Swift compiler versions can import it, and the framework links everything it needs: you add nothing else. ## Add it to an Xcode project 1. Drag `NativeShell.xcframework` (or `NativeShellDev.xcframework` for development builds) into the app target's **Frameworks, Libraries, and Embedded Content**. Choose **Do Not Embed** for the default static frameworks, or **Embed & Sign** for dynamic frameworks built with `--dynamic`. 2. In Swift, `import NativeShell`. 3. In the app's `Info.plist`, set `CADisableMinimumFrameDurationOnPhone` to `YES`: on ProMotion iPhones the app's animations then move at 120 Hz, as scrolling does (apps built by `nsh package` have it). > [!TIP] > Link `NativeShellDev.xcframework` in the Debug configuration and `NativeShell.xcframework` in Release, so only > development builds can connect to a dev server. ## Ship a bundle with the app A Swift app ships TSX apps as bundles. Build the NSH app into a folder and add that folder to the app's resources as a folder reference named `nsh`: ```sh nsh build App.tsx --release --out MyApp/nsh ``` `nsh build` writes: | File | Contents | |---|---| | `bundle.nshc` | The app compiled to bytecode: the fastest to load. | | `bundle.js` | The same app as JS source. | | `bundle.js.map` | Its source map (stack traces point at your `.tsx` files). | | `capabilities.json` | The [capabilities](./sandbox-and-capabilities.md) the app declares, when `nsh.json` has any. | | `assets/` | Images and fonts the app imports, at their paths relative to the entry. | ## Show the app ```swift import NativeShell import UIKit final class EmbedController: UIViewController { private let app = NshAppView() override func viewDidLoad() { super.viewDidLoad() app.translatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints = false app.onError = { message in print("nsh error: \(message)") } view.addSubview(app) NSLayoutConstraint.activate([ app.topAnchor.constraint(equalTo: view.safeAreaLayoutGuide.topAnchor), app.leadingAnchor.constraint(equalTo: view.leadingAnchor), app.trailingAnchor.constraint(equalTo: view.trailingAnchor), app.bottomAnchor.constraint(equalTo: view.bottomAnchor), ]) guard let url = Bundle.main.url(forResource: "bundle", withExtension: "nshc", subdirectory: "nsh") else { return } do { try app.loadBundle(at: url) } catch { print("cannot load: \(error)") } } // Let the embedded app's pages and dialogs decide the status bar. override var preferredStatusBarStyle: UIStatusBarStyle { NshAppView.preferredStatusBarStyle } override var prefersStatusBarHidden: Bool { NshAppView.prefersStatusBarHidden } override var preferredStatusBarUpdateAnimation: UIStatusBarAnimation { NshAppView.preferredStatusBarUpdateAnimation } } ``` The view's size is the app's window: NSH lays the app out at the view's bounds and again whenever they change. Loading again replaces the running app; the app stops when the view is deallocated. The complete sample, a UIKit app that shows an NSH app below its own native header, is `examples/embed-ios/main.swift`. ## `NshAppView` `NshAppView` is a `UIView` subclass isolated to the main actor. | Member | Description | |---|---| | `init(frame: CGRect = .zero, trace: Bool = false)` | Creates the view. `trace` logs the time of every commit. `init?(coder:)` supports storyboards and nibs. | | `onError: ((String) -> Void)?` | Receives fatal app errors (a bundle that fails to load, uncaught JS exceptions, a VM stopped by a limit) on the main thread. Errors are always logged; development builds also show them over the app. | | `limits: NshLimits` | The VM limits of the apps loaded from now on. | | `grantCapabilities(_ json: String?) throws` | The most the apps loaded from now on may do, as JSON in the form of `nsh.json`'s `capabilities`; `nil` grants what each app declares. Throws `NshError` for invalid JSON. | | `locale: Locale?` | The app's language and region in place of the user's: `Intl`, `locale()` and the components follow it at once, and the apps loaded later start in it. `nil` follows the system's. | | `fontScale: CGFloat?` | The text size in place of Dynamic Type's (1 is the default): texts and inputs are laid out again at it and `fontScale()` reads it, at once and for the apps loaded later; lengths keep their size. `nil` follows the system's. | | `setThemeOverrides(_ json: String?) throws` | The host's brand over the app's [theme](./tailwind.md#theme-tokens): a theme file in the format of `nsh.json`'s `"theme"`. Its tokens win over the app's of the same names, in light and dark mode, and the app's others stay. Applies at once and to the apps loaded later; `nil` gives the app its own theme back. Throws `NshError` for a file that does not parse. | | `storageDirectory: URL?` | Where the apps loaded from now on keep their [storage](../modules/nsh.md#storage); `nil`: `Library/Application Support/nsh/`, by the app's own id. | | `cacheOptions: NshCacheOptions` | Where the apps loaded from now on keep their caches, the [images they download](./images-and-assets.md#kept-on-disk), and how much each keeps: `location` `.system` (`Library/Caches/nsh`, each app in ``), `.directory(URL)` or `.off`; `images` `.default` (256 MB), `.maxSize(megabytes:)` or `.off`. | | `loadBundle(at url: URL) throws` | Runs a bundle written by `nsh build`. Assets come from `assets/` next to it; `bundle.js.map` and `capabilities.json` next to it are read too. | | `run(_ package: NshPackage)` | Runs a verified signed package (see below). A package runs once. | | `loadPackage(at:trust:) async throws -> NshPackage.Info` | Verifies the package at a URL off the main thread, then runs it. Throws why it was refused; the running app stays. | | `connectDevServer(_ url: URL) throws` | Development: loads from a `nsh dev` server and reloads on every change. Throws with `NativeShell.xcframework`, which has no development support. | | `register(component:_:)` | Registers a [native component](./native-components.md). | | `params: [String: Any]` | The launch parameters of the apps loaded from now on: the app reads them at start as `host.params` ([`host`](../modules/nsh.md#host)). | | `send(_ name: String, _ data: Any? = nil)` | Sends an event to the app (`host.on(name, …)`); kept until it listens, or for the next app while none runs. | | `handle(_ name: String, _ handler:)` | Handles the app's calls (`host.call`) and posts (`host.post`) of `name` on the main thread: `{ data, reply in … }`, or an `async throws` function `{ data in … }` whose result answers the call. | | `removeHandler(_ name: String)` | Removes the handler of `name`: the app's calls of it fail at once. | | `static preferredStatusBarStyle`, `prefersStatusBarHidden`, `preferredStatusBarUpdateAnimation` | What the running apps asked for (their pages' and dialogs' `statusBar`, `nsh.json`'s default): return them from the hosting view controller's overrides. | > [!IMPORTANT] > `bundle.nshc` (bytecode) loads only from inside the app bundle. QuickJS does not validate bytecode, so bytecode from > anywhere else could corrupt memory: for a file outside the app bundle, load `bundle.js` (JS source), or better, a > [signed package](./signed-packages.md). `limits`, `grantCapabilities`, `storageDirectory` and `cacheOptions` apply from the next load: set them before `loadBundle` / `run`. Each app keeps its storage under its own id with no setting: a signed package under the id its release key's certificate vouches for, a bundle under the `id` of its `nsh.json` (`app.json` next to it, written by `nsh build`). Set `storageDirectory` to keep an app's data somewhere of the host's choosing: ```swift app.storageDirectory = FileManager.default .urls(for: .applicationSupportDirectory, in: .userDomainMask)[0] .appendingPathComponent("nsh/com.example.orders") try app.loadBundle(at: url) ``` ## Talking to the app The view and the app it runs talk through a channel of their own ([`host`](../modules/nsh.md#host)): launch parameters the app reads at start, events from the host app, and calls and posts from the app, with JSON data (Foundation objects on this side). It needs no view in the app and no native component. ```swift // Before loading: what the app opens first (`host.params` in TSX). app.params = ["conversation": notification.conversationID] try app.loadBundle(at: url) // The app's `await host.call("user.profile", { id })`: return the answer, or throw to reject it. app.handle("user.profile") { data in let id = (data as? [String: Any])?["id"] as? Int ?? 0 let profile = try await api.profile(id: id) return ["id": id, "name": profile.name] } // A handler that answers later, from any thread, with its reply. app.handle("photo.pick") { _, reply in picker.present { url in if let url { reply.resolve(url.absoluteString) } else { reply.reject("cancelled") } } } // The app's `host.post("analytics", …)`: no answer. app.handle("analytics") { data, _ in analytics.log(data) } // Later: the app hears `host.on("conversation.open", …)`. app.send("conversation.open", ["id": tapped.conversationID]) ``` Handlers run on the main thread; a call waits for its answer in the app without blocking either side. A reply released unanswered fails the call, and a call of a name with no handler fails at once. Events of names the app does not listen to yet are kept until it does, and events sent while no app runs (before `loadBundle`, during a reload) go to the next one, so a notification tapped while the app starts still reaches it. ## Theme overrides One app embedded in several branded host apps takes each host's brand: the host gives the tokens its brand changes, as a theme file in the format of `nsh.json`'s `"theme"` (shadcn/ui's `cssVars`, values as CSS writes them). They win over the app's tokens of the same names; the app's other tokens stay. Give a token its dark-mode value under `dark` (one set only under `light` or `theme` is that color in both modes): ```swift try app.setThemeOverrides(""" { "cssVars": { "theme": { "radius": "0.75rem" }, "light": { "primary": "#e11d48", "primary-foreground": "#ffffff" }, "dark": { "primary": "#fb7185", "primary-foreground": "#1c1917" } } } """) try app.loadBundle(at: url) ``` Call it before or after loading: classes such as `bg-primary` and `rounded-(--radius)` restyle at once, and every app loaded later starts with the overrides in its first frame. `setThemeOverrides(nil)` gives the app its own theme back. ## Links the app opens The URLs the app opens ([`openUrl`](../modules/nsh.md#openurl), a `TextView`'s links with `links="open"`) reach `onOpenURL` first, on the main thread: return `true` when the host app handled the URL, such as by routing it through its own router, and `false` for the system to open it with `UIApplication.open`. Without `onOpenURL` the system opens every URL. URLs reach it after the app's `openUrl` capability allowed them. ```swift app.onOpenURL = { url in // The host app's own links open in the host app. if url.scheme == "lb" || url.host == "longbridge.com" { router.open(url) return true } return false } ``` ## Limits ```swift app.limits = NshLimits(memoryMB: 128, callBudget: 1, maxNodes: 50_000) ``` | `NshLimits` field | Default | Meaning | |---|---|---| | `memoryMB: UInt32?` | 256 | JS heap in MB. Running out stops the app. | | `stackKB: UInt32?` | 4096 (also the maximum) | Interpreter stack in KB. Deeper recursion throws a `RangeError`. | | `loadBudget: TimeInterval?` | 10 s | Time to evaluate the bundle. | | `callBudget: TimeInterval?` | 2 s | Time of any other call into JS (one event, one timer, one frame). An overrun call is cut off. | | `maxNodes: UInt32?` | 200 000 | Nodes the app may keep. | `nil` keeps the default. What each limit does when it is hit: [Sandbox and capabilities](./sandbox-and-capabilities.md). ## Capabilities An app declares what it may reach in its `nsh.json`; the embedding app can grant less. A request must be allowed by both: ```swift try app.grantCapabilities(""" { "network": { "hosts": ["api.example.com", "*.cdn.example.com"] }, "webview": { "hosts": ["help.example.com"] } } """) try app.loadBundle(at: url) ``` Here the app may not set the status bar (no `statusBar`), even if its `nsh.json` asks for it. Details: [Sandbox and capabilities](./sandbox-and-capabilities.md). ## Signed packages To run code the app downloads (updates, third-party mini apps), use [signed packages](./signed-packages.md): `nsh publish` writes a `.nshpkg` signed by a release key that your root key certified, and the app verifies it before running it. ```swift let support = FileManager.default.urls(for: .applicationSupportDirectory, in: .userDomainMask)[0] let trust = try NshTrust(stateDirectory: support.appendingPathComponent("nsh")) try trust.addRoot(rootPublicKey) // the contents of root.pub from `nsh keygen` Task { do { let info = try await app.loadPackage(at: downloadedFile, trust: trust) print("running \(info.id) \(info.version) (build \(info.build))") } catch { print("refused: \(error)") // the running app stays } } ``` To verify first and run later, split the two steps: ```swift let package = try await trust.openPackage(at: downloadedFile) // verifies off the main thread // ... decide, ask the user, ... app.run(package) ``` | API | Description | |---|---| | `NshTrust(stateDirectory: URL) throws` | Opens or creates the trust store. Its state (newest revocation list, highest build accepted per app) persists there, and packages' assets are extracted under it. Trusts no key until `addRoot`. Thread-safe. | | `addRoot(_ publicKey: String) throws` | Trusts a root public key (base64, the contents of a `.pub` file). An iOS app with Rust code links your crate and the `nsh-platform-ios` crate and shows your root in an `AppView` ([Embedding a Rust app](#embedding-a-rust-app)). A Swift app links `NativeShell.xcframework`, a framework with a Swift module: you create an `NshAppView` (a `UIView`), add it anywhere in your view hierarchy and load a TSX app or a signed package into it. ---
title: Project structure
description: The files of an NSH app in Rust or TSX, every key of nsh.json, the TypeScript setup in .nsh/types, assets, and how modules and packages are imported.
order: 5
group: start
---

# Project structure

An NSH app is a directory with an `nsh.json` and its code: a Rust crate whose root component `nsh.json` names, or a TSX entry module, or both. Everything else (more modules, images, fonts, JSON files) is found from there: a crate's modules and its `assets/` directory, or the files the TSX entry imports, so there is no file list to maintain.

An app written in Rust is a Cargo project:

```text
my-app/
├── nsh.json           name, id, version, icon, the crate ("rust") and its root component ("root"), theme
├── Cargo.toml         the crate: nsh-core, nsh-base and your dependencies
├── src/
│   ├── lib.rs         the root component and the crate's UI set (#[native_module])
│   ├── main.rs        cargo run: the root on this machine's desktop backend
│   └── screens/       your own modules (any layout you like)
├── assets/            files the crate ships: asset!("logo@2x.png"), fonts
├── .gitignore         .nsh/ and target/
├── .nsh/              generated: the runners' sources, test entries, build output (.nsh/out)
└── target/            Cargo's build directory
```

A TSX app is an entry and the modules it imports:

```text
my-app/
├── App.tsx            the entry module: calls mount()
├── App.test.tsx       its tests (nsh test)
├── nsh.json           name, id, version, icon, Tailwind theme, capabilities
├── tsconfig.json      TypeScript settings for editors
├── .gitignore         .nsh/ and target/
├── components/        your own modules (any layout you like)
│   └── Header.tsx
├── assets/
│   ├── logo@2x.png    imported images
│   └── Inter.ttf      imported fonts
└── .nsh/              generated: type declarations, development host builds, test entries, build output (.nsh/out)
```

An app with both lists its crates in `"rust"` and has a TSX entry that imports them ([Building with Rust](./rust.md#extending-a-rust-app-with-tsx)).

Every command takes the app's directory or its entry as its argument (`nsh run my-app`, `nsh run my-app/App.tsx`). The directory of `nsh.json` and the entry is the app's root: `nsh.json` is read from there, asset paths are relative to it, and `.nsh/` is written there. In a Rust app (`nsh.json` `"root"`), the directory runs the root component; naming a TSX entry runs that instead.

## The root component

A Rust app's root is a component of its crate, which `nsh.json`'s `"root"` names by its path in the crate (`App`, `shell::Gallery`). A TSX entry is a normal module that ends by rendering the root component:

```rust tabs
// src/lib.rs; nsh.json: { "rust": ".", "root": "App" }
mod screens;

use nsh_core::prelude::*;

/// What a TSX entry may import from the crate.
#[native_module("my-app/native")]
fn native(registry: &mut Registry) {
    registry.register::<App>().assets(assets!());
}

#[component]
pub fn App() -> impl IntoElement {
    screens::home()
}
```

```tsx tabs
// App.tsx
import { mount } from "nsh";
import { Home } from "./components/Home";

function App() {
  return <Home />;
}

mount(App);
```

`nsh run` and `nsh package` mount a Rust root on every platform, with no QuickJS. In TSX, `mount(component, props?)` renders the component into the app's surface and returns a function that removes it again; an app calls it once. Code at the top level of the entry runs when the bundle loads, before the first frame.

## nsh.json

`nsh.json` sits in the app's root. `nsh init` writes `name`, `id`, `version` and `build`, and for a Rust app the crate and its root component:

```json
{
  "name": "Gallery",
  "id": "com.example.gallery",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "build": 1,
  "rust": ".",
  "root": "App",
  "theme": "theme.json"
}
```

Every other key is optional; a TSX app may also leave out the four. A TSX app's `nsh.json` might read:

```json
{
  "name": "Gallery",
```

## tsconfig.json and .nsh/types

NSH does not need `node_modules`. Instead, every command that builds the app (`init`, `build`, `test`, `dev`, `run`, `package`, `publish`, `check`) writes the TypeScript declarations of everything NSH provides into `.nsh/types`, and NSH's TypeScript settings into `.nsh/tsconfig.json`. The app's `tsconfig.json` extends them:

```json
{
  "extends": "./.nsh/tsconfig.json",
  "include": ["**/*.ts", "**/*.tsx"]
}
```

`.nsh/tsconfig.json` points the `nsh` imports and your app's crates to `.nsh/types`, includes the globals, asset and token declarations, and sets the compiler options NSH apps use (`lib`, `jsx`, `strict`, ...). NSH keeps it current: when a new version adds a library or a path, your app has it with the next build, and your `tsconfig.json` stays as you wrote it. | `types.d.ts` | Styles (`ViewStyle`, `TextStyle`, ...), every element's props and events, the refs (`ViewRef`, `InputRef`, ...: what a `ref` receives) |
| `jsx-runtime.d.ts` | The JSX runtime TypeScript resolves through `jsxImportSource` (the `JSX` namespace) |
| `globals.d.ts` | `If` and `Each`; `console`, timers, `requestAnimationFrame`, `fetch` and the other [global APIs](../modules/globals.md) |
| `assets.d.ts` | What importing an image or font gives |
| `tokens.d.ts` | `Tokens`: the app's design tokens, from its `"theme"`, which type [`token()`](../modules/nsh.md#token) |
| `mobile.d.ts`, `desktop.d.ts` | One file per module (`nsh/mobile`, `nsh/desktop`) |
| `base.d.ts` | `nsh/base` |

`lib` is `ES2023` without `DOM`: there is no `document` or `window`. The files in `.nsh` are regenerated (only when their contents change), so do not edit them and do not commit them; `.gitignore` already excludes `.nsh/`. An app made by an earlier `nsh init` gets the new `tsconfig.json` with its next build when its own is NSH's template, unchanged; NSH prints a line saying so. A `tsconfig.json` you changed is yours: `nsh check` points out when it does not extend `./.nsh/tsconfig.json`, and you add the `extends` line and remove the options it sets.

## Modules

A Rust app's code is its crate's modules (`mod screens;`), and its dependencies come from crates.io like any crate's; NSH's own crates are `nsh-core` (the primitives, signals and typed styles, `use nsh_core::prelude::*`) and `nsh-base` (the base components and the theme).

In TSX, split the app into as many `.ts` and `.tsx` modules as you like and import them with relative paths; the extension may be left out:

```tsx
import { Header } from "./components/Header";
import { formatPrice } from "./lib/format";
import strings from "./strings.json";
```

All of them are bundled into one script. JSON files import as their parsed value.

### Loading code on demand

`import()` of one of the app's modules returns a promise of its exports, as in a browser:

```tsx
const open = async () => {
  const { Settings } = await import("./screens/Settings");
  screen.set(() => Settings);
};
```

Apps on devices ship one bundle, so the module is already there and the promise resolves at once. A web app published split (`nsh build --split`) gets the module, and what only it uses, as a separate file that is downloaded the first time `import()` asks for it ([Web](./web.md#split-bundles)). The specifier must be a literal relative path: the bundler has to see which module is meant.

Imports of `nsh` and `nsh/...` are not bundled: the runtime provides them natively.

|---|---|

| `nsh/base` | The unstyled foundation of an app's UI: navigation stacks and their pages (`NavStack`, `NavPage`, `createNavStack`), dialogs (`Dialog`), a press target (`Button`), a text input (`Input`) and the system's alert dialog (`AlertDialog`); pages and dialogs set the status bar (`statusBar`) ([reference](../modules/nsh-base.md)) |
| `nsh/mobile` | What iOS and Android have: `TabBar`, `InputAccessoryView` (iOS), `BackHandler` (Android) ([reference](../modules/nsh-mobile.md)) |

NSH needs nothing from npm, but the bundler resolves bare imports from a `node_modules` directory if you install packages with a package manager. Packages that touch the DOM do not work: there is none.

A package whose browser build uses the DOM often has another build for workers or React Native. `resolve.conditions` picks the export conditions packages resolve with, in place of the default `["browser"]`: `import`, `require`, `module` and `default` always apply, and without `browser` packages resolve through their `module` and `main` fields. `resolve.alias` replaces an import: by a path relative to `nsh.json` (`./` or `../`), another package, or `false` for an empty module. "resolve": {

```json
  "alias": { "dom-only-helper": "./shims/helper.ts", "node-polyfill": false }

```

```ts
// shims/aliases.d.ts
declare module "node-polyfill";
```

`solid-js` cannot be imported: the bundler refuses it and points to `nsh`'s own `signal`, `computed` and `effect`, which replace it.

## Assets

Images and fonts ship with the app. A Rust crate reads each file of its `assets/` directory at compile time with `asset!`, and ships them all with `registry.assets(assets!())` in its `#[native_module]` function; TSX imports them like modules, and the bundler records each imported file (and an image's pixel-density variants). `nsh build` copies them to `.nsh/out/assets/`, `nsh package` puts them in the app, and during development they are served to the app.

```rust tabs
use nsh_core::element::{FontAsset, ImageAsset, asset};

const LOGO: ImageAsset = asset!("logo@2x.png");      // its url, and its size: 64×64 points
const INTER: FontAsset = asset!("Inter.ttf");        // its uri, and its family: "Inter"

image(LOGO)
text("Hello").font_family(INTER.family)
```

```tsx tabs
import { Image, Text } from "nsh";
import logo from "./assets/logo@2x.png";   // { url: "asset:/assets/logo@2x.png", size: { width: 64, height: 64 } }
import Inter from "./assets/Inter.ttf";     // "Inter"

<Image src={logo} />
<Text style={{ fontFamily: Inter }}>Hello</Text>
```

A file without a suffix also ships its `@1.5x`–`@4x` siblings, listed in `scales`, and the screen's variant is loaded ([pixel densities](./images-and-assets.md#pixel-densities)). |
| `.svg` | An `ImageAsset` sized in points by the SVG's `width` and `height` (or `viewBox`). |
| `.ttf`, `.otf`, `.woff`, `.woff2` | The font's family name, a string. The font is registered before the first frame. |
| `.json` | The parsed JSON |

See [Images and assets](./images-and-assets.md) and [Fonts](./fonts.md).

`.nsh/tsconfig.json` adds `"ESNext.Disposable"`, which declares `using` declarations and `Symbol.dispose`, which the runtime has: `using account = new Account()` frees a [Rust class](./rust.md)'s value at the end of the block. Its `jsxImportSource: "nsh"` and `jsx: "preserve"` only matter to the editor: NSH compiles JSX with its own compiler, whatever the `tsconfig.json` says. TypeScript is checked by your editor or by `nsh check`; the other commands strip types without checking them.

An app made by an earlier `nsh init` gets the new `tsconfig.json` with its next build when its own is NSH's template, unchanged; NSH prints a line saying so. A `tsconfig.json` you changed is yours: `nsh check` points out when it does not extend `./.nsh/tsconfig.json`, and you add the `extends` line and remove the options it sets.

## Modules

A Rust app's code is its crate's modules (`mod screens;`), and its dependencies come from crates.io like any crate's; NSH's own crates are `nsh-core` (the primitives, signals and typed styles, `use nsh_core::prelude::*`) and `nsh-base` (the base components and the theme).

In TSX, split the app into as many `.ts` and `.tsx` modules as you like and import them with relative paths; the extension may be left out:

```tsx
import { Header } from "./components/Header";
import { formatPrice } from "./lib/format";
import strings from "./strings.json";
```

All of them are bundled into one script. JSON files import as their parsed value.

### Loading code on demand

`import()` of one of the app's modules returns a promise of its exports, as in a browser:

```tsx
const open = async () => {
  const { Settings } = await import("./screens/Settings");
  screen.set(() => Settings);
};
```

Apps on devices ship one bundle, so the module is already there and the promise resolves at once. A web app published split (`nsh build --split`) gets the module, and what only it uses, as a separate file that is downloaded the first time `import()` asks for it ([Web](./web.md#split-bundles)). The specifier must be a literal relative path: the bundler has to see which module is meant.

### NSH's modules

Imports of `nsh` and `nsh/...` are not bundled: the runtime provides them natively.

| Module | What it has |
|---|---|
| `nsh` | Reactivity (`signal`, `computed`, `effect`, ...), `mount`, `split`, `context`; the primitives `View`, `Text`, `Scroll`, `Image`, `List`, `Canvas`, `WebView`, `Video` (`View`'s `selectable` for text selection); safe area insets (`safeArea`, `safeAreaInsets`) and the software keyboard (`Keyboard`, `keyboardFrame`); native animations; `PanResponder`; the environment (`platform`, `windowSize`, `colorScheme`, `fontScale`, `pixelRatio`, `locale`); screen reader and reduce motion state, announcements; the clipboard, the photo picker, storage, the host channel, keyboard shortcuts; components and functions the embedding app registers ([reference](../modules/nsh.md)) |
| `nsh/base` | The unstyled foundation of an app's UI: navigation stacks and their pages (`NavStack`, `NavPage`, `createNavStack`), dialogs (`Dialog`), a press target (`Button`), a text input (`Input`) and the system's alert dialog (`AlertDialog`); pages and dialogs set the status bar (`statusBar`) ([reference](../modules/nsh-base.md)) |
| `nsh/mobile` | What iOS and Android have: `TabBar`, `InputAccessoryView` (iOS), `BackHandler` (Android) ([reference](../modules/nsh-mobile.md)) |
| `nsh/desktop` | What macOS, Windows and Linux have: `Window`, `titleBar`, `Menu` ([reference](../modules/nsh-desktop.md)) |

The [modules reference](../modules/index.md) documents each one. Importing a module NSH does not have (`nsh/foo`) is a build error. So is a name your code uses that the module does not export (`import { Buton } from "nsh/base"`): the error points at the import and names the closest export (``did you mean `Button`?``). Names used only as types are checked by `nsh check`.

### npm packages

NSH needs nothing from npm, but the bundler resolves bare imports from a `node_modules` directory if you install packages with a package manager. Packages resolve their browser builds, because the runtime provides web APIs (`fetch`, streams, `URL`, `TextEncoder`, ...) and not Node's (`fs`, `Buffer`, `process`). Packages that touch the DOM do not work: there is none.

A package whose browser build uses the DOM often has another build for workers or React Native. `resolve.conditions` picks the export conditions packages resolve with, in place of the default `["browser"]`: `import`, `require`, `module` and `default` always apply, and without `browser` packages resolve through their `module` and `main` fields. `resolve.alias` replaces an import: by a path relative to `nsh.json` (`./` or `../`), another package, or `false` for an empty module. TypeScript (`nsh check`, editors) types the import as written: a name that is not an installed package gets its types from a `.d.ts` file of the app.

```json
"resolve": {
  "conditions": ["worker"],
  "alias": { "dom-only-helper": "./shims/helper.ts", "node-polyfill": false }
}
```

```ts
// shims/aliases.d.ts
declare module "node-polyfill";
```

`solid-js` cannot be imported: the bundler refuses it and points to `nsh`'s own `signal`, `computed` and `effect`, which replace it.

## Assets

Images and fonts ship with the app. A Rust crate reads each file of its `assets/` directory at compile time with `asset!`, and ships them all with `registry.assets(assets!())` in its `#[native_module]` function; TSX imports them like modules, and the bundler records each imported file (and an image's pixel-density variants). `nsh build` copies them to `.nsh/out/assets/`, `nsh package` puts them in the app, and during development they are served to the app.

```rust tabs
use nsh_core::element::{FontAsset, ImageAsset, asset};

const LOGO: ImageAsset = asset!("logo@2x.png");      // its url, and its size: 64×64 points
const INTER: FontAsset = asset!("Inter.ttf");        // its uri, and its family: "Inter"

image(LOGO)
text("Hello").font_family(INTER.family)
```

```tsx tabs
import { Image, Text } from "nsh";
import logo from "./assets/logo@2x.png";   // { url: "asset:/assets/logo@2x.png", size: { width: 64, height: 64 } }
import Inter from "./assets/Inter.ttf";     // "Inter"

<Image src={logo} />
<Text style={{ fontFamily: Inter }}>Hello</Text>
```

| Extension | Import gives |
|---|---|
| `.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.gif`, `.webp`, `.heic` | An `ImageAsset`: `{ url, size, scales? }`, sized in points. An `@2x` / `@3x` suffix divides the pixel size by 2 / 3. A file without a suffix also ships its `@1.5x`–`@4x` siblings, listed in `scales`, and the screen's variant is loaded ([pixel densities](./images-and-assets.md#pixel-densities)). |
| `.svg` | An `ImageAsset` sized in points by the SVG's `width` and `height` (or `viewBox`). |
| `.ttf`, `.otf`, `.woff`, `.woff2` | The font's family name, a string. The font is registered before the first frame. |
| `.json` | The parsed JSON |

See [Images and assets](./images-and-assets.md) and [Fonts](./fonts.md).

## Generated directories

- **`.nsh/`**: everything NSH generates: the type declarations (`.nsh/types`), the sources of a Rust app's runners (`.nsh/rust`), what `nsh run` installs on simulators and devices (the Catalyst host app, the Android development APK), and `.nsh/out`, the default output of `nsh build` (`bundle.js`, `bundle.js.map`, `bundle.nshc`, `capabilities.json`, `assets/`; for a Rust app, `app.json` and `assets/`) and `nsh package` (`.app`, `.ipa`, `.apk`, a site); `-o` writes elsewhere. Safe to delete; it is recreated.
- **`target/`**: Cargo's build directory for an app's crates and runners (or `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`).

# Building UI in Rust with nsh_base

Read [rust.md](rust.md) first. This page goes family by family: the real constructor, the props and events that matter,
one snippet, and what trips people up. Full prop tables and Rust examples are at
`https://nsh.dev/elements/{name}.md` (`website/elements/` in an NSH checkout).
Check the project’s resolved crate source when its version differs from the site.

Host elements come from `nsh_core::prelude`: `view`, `text`, `scroll`, `image`, `svg`, `virtual_list`, `canvas`,
`video`, `web_view`. Everything else comes from `nsh_base`, including `input`, which the prelude does **not** export.

## Rules for all of nsh_base

- **It has no look.** Each base component provides behavior: focus, keyboard, placement, what screen readers hear. A
  `button()` with no styles is an invisible box the size of its child. Wrap each one once in your own `ui/` module.
- **Parts draw nothing until styled.** A part is reached by a `*_style(|s| ..)` or `*_class("..")` prop, not by the
  element's own methods. The element's own `.bg(..)`, `.px_4()` style its root only. A `switch()` with no `track_style`
  and `thumb_style` shows only its label. A `tabs()` indicator with no `indicator_style` does not exist visually. A
  `menu_separator()` with no height and background is zero points tall. A `select()` popup with no `popup_style` has no
  background, so rows float over the page.
- **Popups and sheets paint nothing behind their content.** The popup is yours: give it `.bg`, `.rounded`, `.shadow_*`.
- **`*_style` closures get a `StyleRefinement`**, so `.checked(|s| ..)`, `.selected(..)`, `.active(..)` work inside them.
  Use state styles there, not a signal.
- **Some states are reachable only by class** on parts the app does not build: `.item_class("focus:bg-accent
  selected:font-medium disabled:opacity-50")`. That is the case for writing a class string in Rust.

7	# Building UI in Rust with nsh_base
8	
9	Read [rust.md](rust.md) first. This page goes family by family: the real constructor, the props and events that matter,
10	one snippet, and what trips people up. Full prop tables and Rust examples are at
11	`https://nsh.dev/elements/{name}.md` (`website/elements/` in an NSH checkout).
12	Check the project’s resolved crate source when its version differs from the site.
13	
14	Host elements come from `nsh_core::prelude`: `view`, `text`, `scroll`, `image`, `svg`, `virtual_list`, `canvas`,
15	`video`, `web_view`. Everything else comes from `nsh_base`, including `input`, which the prelude does **not** export.
16	
17	## Rules for all of nsh_base
18	
19	- **It has no look.** Each base component provides behavior: focus, keyboard, placement, what screen readers hear. A
20	  `button()` with no styles is an invisible box the size of its child. Wrap each one once in your own `ui/` module.
21	- **Parts draw nothing until styled.** A part is reached by a `*_style(|s| ..)` or `*_class("..")` prop, not by the
22	  element's own methods. The element's own `.bg(..)`, `.px_4()` style its root only. A `switch()` with no `track_style`
23	  and `thumb_style` shows only its label. A `tabs()` indicator with no `indicator_style` does not exist visually. A
24	  `menu_separator()` with no height and background is zero points tall. A `select()` popup with no `popup_style` has no
25	  background, so rows float over the page.
26	- **Popups and sheets paint nothing behind their content.** The popup is yours: give it `.bg`, `.rounded`, `.shadow_*`.
27	- **`*_style` closures get a `StyleRefinement`**, so `.checked(|s| ..)`, `.selected(..)`, `.active(..)` work inside them.
28	  Use state styles there, not a signal.
29	- **Some states are reachable only by class** on parts the app does not build: `.item_class("focus:bg-accent
30	  selected:font-medium disabled:opacity-50")`. That is the case for writing a class string in Rust.
31	- **Controlled or not.** `open`, `value` and `checked` are the owner's when set, so follow the event or nothing appears to
32	  happen. `open: Prop<Option<bool>>`: leave it out and the component keeps its own, or use `.default_open(true)`.
33	- **Setter types follow the field.** A `Prop<Option<T>>` takes `T` for text (`.placeholder("x")`), but a closure must
34	  return the `Option`: `.value(move || Some(tags.get()))`. A `Prop<SelectValue>` takes `Option<SharedString>` through
35	  `SelectValue`'s `From`.
36	
37	## Buttons and links
38	
39	`button()`: `disabled`, `selected`, `selected_style`, `accessibility_label`, `role`, `hit_slop`; `on_press`,
40	`on_press_down`, `on_press_up`. `link()`: `href`, `open_with`, `disabled`, `current`, `accessibility_label`, `hit_slop`;
41	`on_open(&SharedString)`, `on_press`.
42	
43	```rust
44	use nsh_base::{button, link, theme};
45	use nsh_core::prelude::*;
46	
47	/// The app's button: wrap once, use everywhere.
48	pub fn primary(label: impl IntoReactive<SharedString>, on_press: impl Fn() + 'static) -> impl IntoElement {
49	    button()
50	        .on_press(on_press)
51	        .h_9()
52	        .px_4()
53	        .items_center()
54	        .justify_center()
55	        .rounded(move || theme().radius)
56	        .bg(move || theme().primary)
57	        .active(|s| s.opacity(0.85))
58	        .focus(|s| s.outline(px(2.0)).outline_color(move || theme().ring))
59	        .disabled_style(|s| s.opacity(0.5))
60	        .child(text(label).text_sm().text_color(move || theme().primary_foreground))
61	}
62	
63	pub fn docs() -> impl IntoElement {
64	    link()
65	        .href("https://nsh.dev/docs")
66	        .text_color(move || theme().primary)
67	        .underline()
68	        .hover(|s| s.opacity(0.8))
69	        .child(text("Read the docs"))
70	}
71	```
72	
73	- Use `button()`, not `view().on_press(..)`, for anything a keyboard or screen reader must reach. `view().on_press` has
74	  no role or focus until you add them.
75	- No built-in press feedback on any platform. Without `.active(..)`, a press looks like nothing happened.
76	- Keep touch targets 44 points on phones. `.hit_slop(EdgeInsets::all(px(10.0)))` grows a small icon's target.
77	- An icon-only button needs `.accessibility_label("Close")`. Tests can then use it as a selector as well.
78	- A link with `href` opens it itself and reports `on_open`. Do not also call `open_url` from `on_press`.
79	
80	## Inputs, forms and keyboard
81	
82	`input()` setters: `value`, `default_value`, `placeholder`, `placeholder_color`, `caret_color`, `selection_color`,
83	`masked`, `multiline`, `readonly`, `max_length`, `keyboard_type`, `return_key_type`, `submit_behavior`, `auto_capitalize`,
84	`auto_correct`, `auto_fill`, `auto_focus`, `selected_range`. Listeners: `on_change(&str)`, `on_submit(&str)`, `on_focus`,
85	`on_blur`, `on_key_press(&str)`, `on_selection_change`, `on_composition_change`, `on_paste`.
86	
87	```rust
88	use nsh_base::{input, theme};
89	use nsh_core::{element::AutoFill, prelude::*};
90	
91	/// The app's text field.
92	fn field(placeholder: &'static str, value: Signal<String>) -> Input {
93	    input()
94	        .value(move || value.get())
95	        .on_change(move |text: &str| value.set(text.to_owned()))
96	        .placeholder(placeholder)
97	        .placeholder_color(|| color(theme().muted_foreground))
98	        .caret_color(|| color(theme().primary))
99	        .h_9()
100	        .px_3()
101	        .text_sm()
102	        .rounded(move || theme().radius)
103	        .border_1()
104	        .border_color(move || theme().input)
105	        .focus(|s| s.border_color(move || theme().ring))
106	}
107	
108	#[component]
109	pub fn SignIn() -> impl IntoElement {
110	    let email = signal(String::new());
111	    let password = signal(String::new());
112	    let password_field = element_ref();
113	    let can_submit = computed(move || email.with(|e| e.contains('@')) && password.with(|p| !p.is_empty()));
114	    let submit = move || {
115	        if can_submit.get_untracked() {
116	            dismiss_keyboard();
117	            log::info!("sign in {}", email.get_untracked());
118	        }
119	    };
120	    // The form scrolls, so the focused input is kept above the keyboard natively.
121	    scroll()
122	        .flex_1()
123	        .keyboard_dismiss_mode(KeyboardDismissMode::OnDrag)
124	        .keyboard_taps(KeyboardTaps::Handled)
125	        .child(
126	            view()
127	                .p_4()
128	                .gap_3()
129	                .child(
130	                    field("E-mail", email)
131	                        .keyboard_type(KeyboardType::Email)
132	                        .auto_capitalize(AutoCapitalize::None)
133	                        .auto_fill(AutoFill::Email)
134	                        .return_key_type(ReturnKeyType::Next)
135	                        .submit_behavior(SubmitBehavior::Submit)
136	                        .on_submit(move |_: &str| password_field.focus()),
137	                )
138	                .child(
139	                    field("Password", password)
140	                        .element_ref(&password_field)
141	                        .masked(true)
142	                        .return_key_type(ReturnKeyType::Go)
143	                        .on_submit(move |_: &str| submit()),
144	                )
145	                .child(view().on_press(submit).child(text("Sign in"))),
146	        )
147	}
148	
149	/// A key of the app. Goes with the owner, as any listener does.
150	fn shortcuts(find: Signal<bool>) {
151	    on_key("mod+k", move |_| find.set(true));
152	}
153	```
154	
155	- Controlled input: `.value` and `.on_change` together. Without `.on_change` writing the signal, typing is thrown back.
156	  For a value the app never reads while typing, `.default_value` is simpler and avoids a round trip per key.
157	- Do not transform text on a CJK composition. While `on_composition_change` reports composing, do not search or rewrite
158	  `value`: it breaks pinyin. See `website/docs/forms-and-keyboard.md`, "Controlled and uncontrolled inputs".
159	- `placeholder_color`, `caret_color` and `selection_color` take a resolved `Hsla`, not `AdaptiveColor`. Wrap the token in
160	  `color(..)` inside a closure, so that it follows the appearance.
161	- A single-line input's return is `SubmitBehavior::BlurAndSubmit` by default: it loses focus. Use `Submit` to stay focused
162	  while moving to the next field.
163	- In a `scroll`, the keyboard inset is handled natively. For a bar pinned under a list (a chat), use `.pb_keyboard()` on
164	  the screen's root; do not read `keyboard_height()` per frame.
165	- `on_key` takes keystrokes such as `"mod+k"` (`mod` is Command on Apple platforms, Control elsewhere), `"shift+mod+l"`,
166	  `"escape"`, `"f5"`. A keystroke that is not one, or one the platform keeps (Command+Q), **panics**. Desktop platforms fire
167	  them; elsewhere no key does, so never make one the only way to reach an action. `key_label(..)` gives the label to show.
168	- `checkbox()`, `switch()`, `radio_group()`, `slider()`, `number_input()`, `otp_input()`, `time_field()`, `date_picker()`
169	  follow the same controlled pattern: `.checked(signal).on_change(move |v: &bool| signal.set(*v))`. `switch()` needs
170	  `track_style` and `thumb_style` and `checkbox()` needs `indicator_style`, or nothing is drawn. See
171	  `website/elements/switch.md`.
172	
173	## Select and combobox
174	
175	`select()` picks one; `combobox()` types to filter and may pick many. Items are data: `SelectItem::new(value, title)`,
176	with `.disabled(bool)`.
177	
178	| | `select()` | `combobox()` |
179	|---|---|---|
180	| Value | `.value(move \|\| chosen.get())`, an `Option<SharedString>` | `.value(move \|\| Some(chosen.get()))`, a `Vec<SharedString>` |
181	| Listener | `on_change(&Option<SharedString>)` | `on_change(&Vec<SharedString>)`, `on_query_change(&SharedString)` |
182	| The closed control | `.trigger(element)`, a slot you draw | Styles on the element itself, `.input_style(..)`, `.trigger_button(..)` |
183	| Search | `.searchable(true)` | Always |
184	
185	```rust
186	use nsh_base::{SelectEntry, SelectEvent, SelectItem, select, theme};
187	use nsh_core::prelude::*;
188	
189	fn fruit_select() -> impl IntoElement {
190	    let fruit = signal(None::<SharedString>);
191	    let items = vec![SelectItem::new("apple", "Apple"), SelectItem::new("kiwi", "Kiwi").disabled(true)];
192	    select()
193	        .items(items)
194	        .value(move || fruit.get())
195	        .on_change(move |next: &Option<SharedString>| fruit.set(next.clone()))
196	        .on_open_change(|e: &SelectEvent| {
197	            if let SelectEvent::OpenChange(open, reason) = e {
198	                log::debug!("{open} {reason:?}");
199	            }
200	        })
201	        .accessibility_label("Fruit")
202	        .offset(px(4.0))
203	        .popup_style(|s| {
204	            s.p_1()
205	                .rounded_lg()
206	                .border_1()
207	                .border_color(move || theme().border)
208	                .bg(move || theme().popover)
209	                .shadow_md()
210	        })
211	        .item_class("rounded-md focus:bg-accent selected:font-medium disabled:opacity-50")
212	        .render_item(|item: &SelectEntry| view().px_2().py_1p5().child(text(item.title.clone()).text_sm()))
213	        .trigger(
214	            view()
215	                .h_9()
216	                .px_3()
217	                .justify_center()
218	                .rounded_md()
219	                .border_1()
220	                .border_color(move || theme().input)
221	                .child(text(move || fruit.get().unwrap_or("Pick a fruit".into()))),
222	        )
223	}
224	```
225	
226	- Without `.trigger(..)` there is nothing to press. The trigger's text is yours to bind to the value.
227	- `.render_item` runs once per item, like a cell: use `group-selected:`-style states for the look, not a signal read.
228	- On phones and tablets it presents as a sheet, and on desktops as a popup over the trigger. Test with `popup_style`
229	  on both, and do not set a width that assumes one of them.
230	- `popup_style` and `item_class` are the only way to reach those parts; `.bg(..)` on `select()` does nothing to the popup.
231	- On a `combobox()`, `.placeholder(closure)` is how the closed text follows the selection; there is no trigger slot.
232	- For a command palette, use `command()` (`website/elements/command.md`); do not stretch `combobox`.
233	
234	## Dialogs, sheets, popovers, menus, toasts
235	
236	| Need | Use | Mount |
237	|---|---|---|
238	| Native confirm or action sheet | `alert_dialog()..show().await` | A task; no element |
239	| Full native modal (own window layer) | `dialog()` | In `when(open, ..)`; leaving it out dismisses |
240	| Panel sliding from an edge | `sheet()` | Always in the tree, `.open(..)` |
241	| Anchored content | `popover()` | `.trigger(..)`, `.child(..)` |
242	| Commands on a trigger, or on right-click | `menu()`, `context_menu()` | `.trigger(..)`, `menu_item()` children |
243	| Hint on hover | `tooltip()` | Wraps the anchor (`website/elements/tooltip.md`) |
244	| Transient message | `toast_stack()`, `toast()`, `ToastManager` | Mounted once, app-level |
245	
246	```rust
247	use nsh_base::{
248	    OpenChangeReason, PopoverEvent, SheetEvent, alert_dialog, dialog, menu, menu_item, menu_separator, popover, sheet,
249	    theme,
250	};
251	use nsh_core::prelude::*;
252	
253	/// A native confirm. Do this in a task, never by blocking.
254	fn confirm_delete(deleted: Signal<bool>) {
255	    spawn(async move {
256	        let answer = alert_dialog()
257	            .title("Delete the photo?")
258	            .description("This cannot be undone.")
259	            .cancel("cancel", "Cancel")
260	            .destructive("delete", "Delete")
261	            .show()
262	            .await;
263	        if matches!(answer, Ok(r) if r.action.as_deref() == Some("delete")) {
264	            deleted.set(true);
265	        }
266	    });
267	}
268	
269	/// A dialog: in the view while open.
270	fn compose(open: Signal<bool>) -> impl IntoElement {
271	    when(open, move || {
272	        dialog()
273	            .presentation(ModalPresentation::PageSheet)
274	            .on_cancel(move || open.set(false))
275	            .flex_1()
276	            .bg(move || theme().background)
277	            .child(view().flex_1().p_safe_area().child(text("Compose")))
278	    })
279	}
280	
281	/// A sheet: always in the tree, its content made while open.
282	fn filters(open: Signal<bool>) -> impl IntoElement {
283	    sheet()
284	        .open(move || Some(open.get()))
285	        .on_open_change(move |e: &SheetEvent| {
286	            if let SheetEvent::OpenChange(next, _) = e {
287	                open.set(*next);
288	            }
289	        })
290	        .child(view().p_6().rounded_t(px(16.0)).bg(move || theme().card).child(text("Filters")))
291	}
292	
293	fn details() -> impl IntoElement {
294	    popover()
295	        .offset(px(6.0))
296	        .margin(px(8.0))
297	        .trigger(view().px_3().py_2().child(text("Details")))
298	        .on_open_change(|e: &PopoverEvent| {
299	            if let PopoverEvent::OpenChange(_, OpenChangeReason::PressOutside) = e {
300	                log::debug!("dismissed");
301	            }
302	        })
303	        .child(view().w(px(240.0)).p_3().rounded_lg().bg(move || theme().popover).shadow_lg().child(text("Shipped")))
304	}
305	
306	fn file_menu() -> impl IntoElement {
307	    let item = |label: &'static str| {
308	        menu_item()
309	            .on_select(move || log::info!("{label}"))
310	            .px_3()
311	            .py_2()
312	            .rounded_md()
313	            .hover(|s| s.bg(move || theme().accent))
314	            .child(text(label))
315	    };
316	    menu()
317	        .offset(px(4.0))
318	        .popup_style(|s| s.p_1().rounded_lg().bg(move || theme().popover).shadow_md())
319	        .trigger(view().px_3().py_2().child(text("File")))
320	        .child(item("New"))
321	        .child(menu_separator().h(px(1.0)).my_1().bg(move || theme().border))
322	        .child(item("Open"))
323	}
324	```
325	
326	- A `dialog()` has no look or size of its own. Give it `.flex_1()` and a background, and use the safe area inside. Its
327	  `on_cancel` fires on Escape, Android back, a backdrop press and a swipe down; if you do not set `open` false, it stays.
328	- A dialog is a native layer over everything else, the stack's header included. Nothing outside it can draw above it.
329	- `alert_dialog()` uses native buttons, by id. The result's `action` is the id, or `None` when dismissed. Do not write a
330	  custom dialog for a yes-or-no.
331	- A `sheet()`'s children are lazy: a `#[component]` placed in it is made on each opening and disposed after, so state
332	  that must survive closing belongs to the parent. Without `.bg` on the child, the sheet is see-through.
333	- A `popover()` or `menu()` opens from its `.trigger` by itself; do not add an `on_press` to open it. Use `.open(..)` only
334	  when something else must open it, and then follow `on_open_change`.
335	- Inside a menu, `menu_item().on_select` closes the menu after running. `.close_on_select(false)` keeps it for toggles,
336	  with `.checked(..)` and `.indicator(..)`.
337	- Toasts have no one-call API in `nsh_base`. `ToastManager` is headless storage, and `toast_stack` and `toast` draw them.
338	  Build one `toast("Copied")`-style helper around them in your `ui/`, as `website/elements/toast.md` shows. Advance the
339	  manager on an interval and pass `state.is_expanded()` so a hover pauses the timeouts.
340	
341	## Navigation: stacks and pages
342	
343	`nav_stack()`'s children are its `nav_page()`s, bottom to top. **Put a page in to push it, and leave it out to pop.** The
344	stack is state you own: a signal of routes, rendered with `each`.
345	
346	```rust
347	use nsh_base::{nav_page, nav_stack, theme};
348	use nsh_core::prelude::*;
349	
350	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
351	enum Route {
352	    Inbox,
353	    Message(u32),
354	}
355	
356	/// The pages' header on the desktops and the web; iOS and Android draw their own from `title`.
357	fn header(routes: Signal<Vec<Route>>, title: impl IntoReactive<SharedString>) -> impl IntoElement {
358	    view()
359	        .h(px(48.0))
360	        .flex_row()
361	        .items_center()
362	        .gap_3()
363	        .px_4()
364	        .border_b_1()
365	        .border_color(move || theme().border)
366	        .child(when(
367	            move || routes.with(|r| r.len() > 1),
368	            move || {
369	                text("Back").role(AccessibilityRole::Button).on_press(move || {
370	                    routes.update(|r| {
371	                        r.pop();
372	                    })
373	                })
374	            },
375	        ))
376	        .child(text(title).font_weight(FontWeight::SEMIBOLD))
377	}
378	
379	fn inbox(routes: Signal<Vec<Route>>) -> Screen {
380	    nav_page().title("Inbox").header(header(routes, "Inbox")).child(
381	        scroll().flex_1().children((1..=5).map(move |id| {
382	            view()
383	                .p_4()
384	                .on_press(move || routes.update(|r| r.push(Route::Message(id))))
385	                .child(text(format!("Message {id}")))
386	        })),
387	    )
388	}
389	
390	fn message(routes: Signal<Vec<Route>>, id: u32) -> Screen {
391	    let title = format!("Message {id}");
392	    nav_page()
393	        .title(title.clone())
394	        .header(header(routes, title))
395	        .child(view().flex_1().p_4().child(text("The body.")))
396	}
397	
398	#[component]
399	pub fn App() -> impl IntoElement {
400	    let routes = signal(vec![Route::Inbox]);
401	    nav_stack().flex_1().child(each(
402	        routes,
403	        |route: &Route| format!("{route:?}"), // the key: stable per route
404	        move |route, index| {
405	            let page = match route.get_untracked() {
406	                Route::Inbox => inbox(routes),
407	                Route::Message(id) => message(routes, id),
408	            };
409	            // The user went back natively: drop this route and those above it.
410	            page.on_dismiss(move || routes.update(|r| r.truncate(index.get_untracked())))
411	        },
412	    ))
413	}
414	```
415	
416	- To push from anywhere, keep routes that make their own page in a `global`, as `examples/gallery-rs/native/src/nav.rs`
417	  and `shell.rs` (`pushed`) do.
418	- **`.on_dismiss` is required.** A native back or swipe pops the page natively. Without it, your signal still holds the
419	  route, and the stack and your state disagree.
420	- Two routes with one key are one page. A key must identify the page, and the gallery's `nav::push_route` refuses a
421	  duplicate, which also stops a double tap from pushing twice (`examples/gallery-rs/native/src/nav.rs`).
422	- `.header(..)` is what desktops and the web show; `.title` and `.header_right(..)`, `.header_left(..)`,
423	  `.header_title(..)` configure the system header on iOS and Android. Set both when you want the same action everywhere.
424	  `examples/gallery-rs/native/src/ui/parts.rs` (`with_header`) wraps this.
425	- A page's content reads its insets with `cx.insets()` from `Scope`, not `safe_area()`: the page has a header above it.
426	- To ask before leaving: `.pop_on_back(false)` with `.on_back_press(..)`. Set it before the user acts, since it is decided
427	  natively when the system asks. Android's back button outside a stack: `on_back_press(|| { ..; true })`.
428	- `.header_large_title(true)` is an iOS look; gate it with `os() == Os::Ios` (`demos/navigation.rs`, `large_title`).
429	- `presentation`-style modal stacks are dialogs: see `demos/navigation.rs` in the gallery for every kind.
430	- Tabs and other layouts are ordinary composition; a stack inside each tab is fine. Reading `when(desktop, ..)` over the
431	  whole shell remakes it, so keep what is open in signals outside (`shell.rs`).
432	
433	## Tabs
434	
435	`tabs()` is the row, with arrow keys and a roving focus; `tab()` is one button in it. **Tabs do not hold the selection or
436	the panels.** You own which is selected, and you show the panel.
437	
438	```rust
439	use nsh_base::{tab, tabs, theme};
440	use nsh_core::prelude::*;
441	
442	fn sections() -> impl IntoElement {
443	    let section = signal("overview");
444	    let item = move |value: &'static str, label: &'static str| {
445	        let selected = move || section.get() == value;
446	        tab()
447	            .selected(selected)
448	            .on_press(move |_: &()| section.set(value))
449	            .px_3()
450	            .py_2()
451	            .child(text(label).text_sm().text_color(move || {
452	                if selected() { theme().foreground } else { theme().muted_foreground }
453	            }))
454	    };
455	    view()
456	        .gap_4()
457	        .child(
458	            tabs()
459	                .flex_row()
460	                .self_start()
461	                .gap_1()
462	                .p_1()
463	                .rounded(move || theme().radius)
464	                .bg(move || theme().muted)
465	                .indicator_style(|s| s.top_1().bottom_1().rounded_md().bg(move || theme().background))
466	                .child(item("overview", "Overview"))
467	                .child(item("activity", "Activity")),
468	        )
469	        .child(when(move || section.get() == "overview", || text("This week")).otherwise(|| text("Deploys")))
470	}
471	```
472	
473	- The indicator is drawn behind the tabs, and it follows the selected tab natively. It has no size across the row until
474	  `indicator_style` gives it `top`, `bottom` and a background.
475	- Panels in `when` are disposed when switched away, so their scroll offset and drafts are lost. To keep them, keep each
476	  panel mounted and use `.style_when(not_selected, |s| s.hidden())`.
477	- A bottom tab bar is your own UI too: NSH has no native tab bar element.
478	
479	## Lists and virtualized data
480	
481	Use `virtual_list(count, |at| row)` for anything that can grow. The list is native: cells are recycled, and only the rows
482	near the viewport exist.
483	
484	**A cell's closure runs once per cell, not once per row.** A cell shows other rows as it is reused. `at` is a `Position`,
485	and `at.index()` read in a binding is what makes the cell follow.
486	
487	```rust
488	use std::collections::HashSet;
489	
490	use nsh_base::theme;
491	use nsh_core::prelude::*;
492	
493	#[derive(Clone, PartialEq)]
494	struct Post {
495	    id: u32,
496	    title: SharedString,
497	}
498	
499	#[component]
500	fn Feed() -> impl IntoElement {
501	    let posts = signal((0..1000).map(|id| Post { id, title: format!("Post {id}").into() }).collect::<Vec<_>>());
502	    // Per-item state lives in data, by id. Not in a signal in the row.
503	    let liked = signal(HashSet::<u32>::new());
504	    let list = element_ref();
505	    virtual_list(move || posts.with(Vec::len), move |at| {
506	        // The current row's post. A memo, so bindings run only when it changes.
507	        let post = computed(move || posts.with(|p| p.get(at.index()).cloned()));
508	        let id = move || post.with(|p| p.as_ref().map_or(0, |p| p.id));
509	        view()
510	            .flex_row()
511	            .items_center()
512	            .p_4()
513	            .child(text(move || post.with(|p| p.as_ref().map(|p| p.title.clone()).unwrap_or_default())).flex_1())
514	            .child(
515	                text(move || if liked.with(|s| s.contains(&id())) { "♥" } else { "♡" }).on_press(move || {
516	                    liked.update(|s| {
517	                        if !s.remove(&id()) {
518	                            s.insert(id());
519	                        }
520	                    })
521	                }),
522	            )
523	    })
524	    // Identities: required when rows come and go other than at the end.
525	    .keys(move || posts.with(|p| p.iter().map(|p| p.id).collect::<Vec<_>>()))
526	    .estimated_item_size(px(52.0))
527	    .separator(|| view().h(px(1.0)).bg(move || theme().border))
528	    .header(text("Latest").p_4())
529	    .empty(text("Nothing yet").p_4())
530	    .on_load_more(move || log::info!("next page"))
531	    .flex_1()
532	    .element_ref(&list)
533	}
534	```
535	
536	Wrong, and looks right on the first screen:
537	
538	```rust
539	use nsh_core::prelude::*;
540	
541	fn wrong(titles: Signal<Vec<SharedString>>) -> impl IntoElement {
542	    virtual_list(move || titles.with(Vec::len), move |at| {
543	        // Read once: this cell shows the first row it was given, forever.
544	        let title = titles.with(|t| t[at.index()].clone());
545	        // A signal in a cell travels with the cell to the next row.
546	        let expanded = signal(false);
547	        view().on_press(move || expanded.set(true)).child(text(title))
548	    })
549	}
550	```
551	
552	- `.estimated_item_size(..)` should be close to the typical row (default 50): it drives the scroll indicator and jumps.
553	- A list needs a bounded height. `.flex_1()` in a parent that has height, or it collapses.
554	- Rows differ in height freely; they are measured. Use one element shape per cell, and a binding to vary it. For rows of
555	  different kinds, `when` inside the cell works, at a cost on each reuse.
556	- Index with care during a removal. A binding can run while the count changes, so use `p.get(i)` with a fallback, as above,
557	  when rows can be removed.
558	- Layout methods come from `ListLayout`: `.columns(n)`, `.horizontal()`, `.inverted()`, `.alignment(ListAlignment::Bottom)` (chat), `.content_padding(..)`,
559	  `.row_gap(..)`, `.column_gap(..)`, `.viewport(ListViewport::Parent)` (a list inside a page's `scroll`, without nesting
560	  scrollers).
561	- Also on the list: `.sticky_header_indices(..)`, `.initial_scroll_index(..)`, `.on_load_more_at_start(..)`,
562	  `.viewability(..)` with `.on_viewable_items_change(..)`. From a ref: `list.scroll_to_index(i, percentage(0.5), px(0.0),
563	  true)`, `list.scroll_to_end(true)`.
564	- `.columns` changed by a signal: wrap the list in `dynamic` with a keyed list, so nothing of the old layout stays.
565	- `each` in a `scroll` makes every row and keeps it. Fine for tens of rows, not for thousands.
566	
567	`examples/gallery-rs/native/src/demos/lists.rs` has grids, sticky contacts, an inverted chat and pull to refresh.

569	## Scrolling and the safe area
570	
571	`scroll()`, with `Scrollable` methods: `.horizontal()`, `.paging(..)`, `.snap_interval(..)`, `.bounces(..)`, `.scrollbar(..)`,
572	`.keyboard_dismiss_mode(..)`, `.keyboard_taps(..)`, `.refreshing(..)`, `.on_refresh(..)`, `.on_scroll(..)`,
573	`.scroll_value(&animated)`.
574	
575	```rust
576	use nsh_base::theme;
577	use nsh_core::prelude::*;
578	
579	fn page() -> impl IntoElement {
580	    let refreshing = signal(false);
581	    view()
582	        .flex_1()
583	        .bg(move || theme().background)
584	        .child(
585	            scroll()
586	                .flex_1()
587	                .refreshing(refreshing)
588	                .on_refresh(move || refreshing.set(true))
589	                .child(view().p_4().pb_safe_area_plus(px(16.0)).gap_3().child(text("Content"))),
590	        )
591	        .child(view().px_4().pb_safe_area().child(text("A bar under the scroll")))
592	}
593	```
594	
595	- `.flex_1()` on the scroll is nearly always needed. Without a bounded height, it grows with its content and never scrolls.
596	- Style padding and gaps on a child view, as above, not on the scroll: the child is the content.
597	- Do not nest a list in a same-axis `scroll`. Use `.viewport(ListViewport::Parent)`.
598	- Safe area: `.p_safe_area()`, `.px_safe_area()`, `.pt_safe_area()`, `.pb_safe_area()`, `.pt_safe_area_plus(px(20.0))`,
599	  `.pb_safe_area_plus(..)`, as native styles with no binding. `safe_area()` reads the raw insets, and subscribes. Inside a
600	  page or modal use `cx.insets()`.
601	- Let the background extend under the bars: the root paints, and the padded child holds the content.
602	- A `refreshing` signal must be set false by you when the work ends, or the spinner stays.
603	- `.on_scroll` is an event per frame into Rust. To drive a visual from the offset, use `.scroll_value(&animated)` with
604	  `bind_*`, which stays on the UI thread (`demos/scrolling.rs`).
605	
606	## Tables
607	
608	`table()` for a small static table with a table's semantics; `data_table()` for any number of rows and columns.
609	
610	```rust
611	use nsh_base::{
612	    DataTableClasses, DataTableColumn, DataTablePress, DataTableRows, DataTableSort, data_table, table, table_body, table_cell, table_head, table_header,
613	    table_row, theme,
614	};
615	use nsh_core::prelude::*;
616	
617	fn invoices() -> impl IntoElement {
618	    let cell = |label: &'static str| table_cell().w(px(120.0)).px_3().py_2().child(text(label));
619	    table()
620	        .accessibility_label("Recent invoices")
621	        .child(table_header().child(table_row().child(table_head().w(px(120.0)).px_3().child(text("Invoice")))))
622	        .child(table_body().child(table_row().child(cell("INV001"))))
623	}
624	
625	fn column(key: &'static str, title: &'static str, width: f32) -> DataTableColumn {
626	    let mut column = DataTableColumn::default();
627	    column.key = key.into();
628	    column.title = Some(title.into());
629	    column.width = Some(px(width));
630	    column.sortable = true;
631	    column
632	}
633	
634	fn quotes() -> impl IntoElement {
635	    let rows = DataTableRows::new(2).texts("symbol", ["AAPL", "MSFT"]).numbers("change", [1.2, -0.4]);
636	    data_table()
637	        .columns(vec![column("symbol", "Symbol", 120.0), column("change", "Change", 90.0)])
638	        .data(rows)
639	        .row_height(px(32.0))
640	        .stripe(true)
641	        .classes({
642	            let mut classes = DataTableClasses::default();
643	            classes.header = Some("border-b border-border".into());
644	            classes
645	        })
646	        .on_row_press(|_: &DataTablePress| log::debug!("row"))
647	        .on_sort_change(|sort: &Option<DataTableSort>| log::debug!("{}", sort.is_some()))
648	        .h(px(320.0))
649	        .border_1()
650	        .border_color(move || theme().border)
651	}
652	```
653	
654	- `DataTableColumn` and similar are `#[non_exhaustive]`: build with `default()` and assign fields, not a struct literal.
655	- `data_table` fills the box it is given. Give `.flex_1()` or a height, or it has nothing to lay out in.
656	- `DataTableRows` is by column, each of one type. `key` joins a column to its field; a wrong key is an empty column.
657	- Sorting is yours. `on_sort_change` reports the request; sort your data and set `.sort(..)` and `.data(..)`.
658	- Lines, colors and selection feedback come from `.classes(..)` and `.styles(..)`; with none, the table has no dividers.
659	- A table's own width: `table_cell` and `table_head` take the widths. A static table does not virtualize or scroll by
660	  itself; put it in a `scroll().horizontal()` when it can overflow.
661	- `.render_cell(|cell: &DataTableCell| ..)` runs per visible cell. Keep it light.
662	
663	## Editor
664	
665	`editor()` (feature `editor`, on by default) is a code editor with highlighting, folding, search and diagnostics.
666	
667	```rust
668	use nsh_base::{Editor, EditorApi, editor};
669	use nsh_core::prelude::*;
670	
671	fn code() -> impl IntoElement {
672	    let source = signal(SharedString::from("fn main() {}\n"));
673	    let handle = component_ref::<Editor>();
674	    view()
675	        .flex_1()
676	        .child(text("Insert date").on_press(move || {
677	            // The ref's methods: focus, value, set_value, insert, selections, run, ...
678	            if let Some(api) = handle.api::<EditorApi>() {
679	                api.insert("2026-11-05".to_owned());
680	            }
681	        }))
682	        .child(
683	            editor()
684	                .value(move || Some(source.get()))
685	                .language("rust")
686	                .on_change(move |value: &SharedString| source.set(value.clone()))
687	                .read_only(false)
688	                .soft_wrap(true)
689	                .font_size(px(13.0))
690	                .component_ref(&handle)
691	                .flex_1(),
692	        )
693	}
694	```
695	
696	- `.value` takes an `Option`, so its closure returns `Some(..)`. Each keystroke sends the whole text through `on_change`.
697	  For a large file, use `.default_value(..)` and read the text only when saving.
698	- Give it `.flex_1()` or a height. It scrolls itself, so do not put it in a `scroll`.
699	- `font_size`, `line_height` and `font_family` are props, not styles, because the editor measures text itself.
700	- Part colors come from `.classes(..)` and `.styles(..)` (`EditorClasses`, `EditorStyles`).
701	- `language` takes a name, alias, extension or file name (`"rust"`, `"rs"`). See `website/elements/editor.md`. For a
702	  read-only diff, use `diff_view()`.
703	- `rich_editor` is a separate module (feature `rich-editor`): `website/elements/rich-editor.md`.
704	
705	## Text view
706	
707	`text_view()` renders Markdown, HTML or a document natively. Use `text()` for labels; use this for content.
708	
709	```rust
710	use nsh_base::{MarkdownOptions, TextViewCodeAction, TextViewLinkPressEvent, text_view, theme};
711	use nsh_core::prelude::*;
712	
713	fn reply(markdown: Signal<SharedString>, streaming: Signal<bool>) -> impl IntoElement {
714	    text_view()
715	        .markdown(move || Some(markdown.get()))
716	        .options(move || MarkdownOptions { streaming: streaming.get(), ..MarkdownOptions::default() })
717	        .selectable(true)
718	        .code_block_actions(vec![TextViewCodeAction::new("copy").with_label("Copy code")])
719	        .on_link_press(|event: &TextViewLinkPressEvent| log::info!("{}", event.url))
720	        .gap_3()
721	        .text_size(px(15.0))
722	        .line_height(px(22.0))
723	        .text_color(move || theme().foreground)
724	}
725	```
726	
727	- It does not scroll. Put it in a `scroll` or a list row. It has no spacing of its own: `.gap_3()` separates blocks.
728	- `.text_size` and `.text_color` on the element are the base; headings and code come from `.classes(..)` and `.styles(..)`
729	  by part (`TextViewClasses`, `TextViewStyles`, or `provide_context` of `TextViewParts`, as
730	  `examples/gallery-rs/native/src/demos/chat/markdown.rs` does).
731	- Set `MarkdownOptions { streaming: true, .. }` while text is arriving (`.streaming_caret(..)` places a caret), and false
732	  once it ends, as `demos/chat/markdown.rs` does.
733	- `.selectable(true)` is off by default. Links are only reported (`on_link_press`) unless `.links(TextViewLinks::Open)`.
734	- Formulas need feature `math`; without it they show as TeX or through your `render_math`.
735	- `.render_code_block(..)`, `.render_custom(..)` draw parts yourself; they are kept per key while the value stays equal.
736	
737	## Images
738	
739	`image(src)`, where `src` is an asset, a URL, or a signal of either. `svg(src)` for vectors.
740	
741	```rust
742	use nsh_core::prelude::*;
743	
744	const LOGO: ImageAsset = asset!("logo.png");
745	
746	fn avatar(url: Signal<String>) -> impl IntoElement {
747	    let failed = signal(false);
748	    view()
749	        .flex_row()
750	        .gap_3()
751	        .child(image(LOGO).size(px(32.0)))
752	        .child(
753	            image(move || url.get())
754	                .placeholder(LOGO)
755	                .object_fit(ResizeMode::Cover)
756	                .size(px(64.0))
757	                .rounded_full()
758	                .label("Profile picture")
759	                .on_error(move |_: &str| failed.set(true)),
760	        )
761	}
762	```
763	
764	- `asset!("logo.png")` is relative to the crate's `assets/` directory, checked at compile time. Register the assets with
765	  `registry.assets(assets!())` in `#[native_module]` (`examples/gallery-rs/native/src/lib.rs`, `assets.rs`).
766	- Give an image a size: `.size(..)`, or `.w(..)` with an aspect ratio. An unsized remote image has no size until loaded,
767	  so the layout jumps.
768	- `.object_fit(ResizeMode::Cover)` and `.rounded_*` work together; the corner clip is native.
769	- A screenshot test cannot show images in headless runs: they are not loaded there. See
770	  [rust-testing.md](rust-testing.md).

## From Rust components

Rust components, `#[module]` functions and `#[class]` members call `fetch` from a task: `spawn` in a component, `resource` for a value the UI shows, or an `async fn` exported to TSX, which TSX awaits as a Promise. A request is a URL or an `HttpRequest` (`HttpRequest::get(url)`, `HttpRequest::post(url, body)`, `.header(name, value)`), and its response arrives whole. The task owns the request: dropping it, or the component that spawned it going away, cancels the request. It uses the same network stack and capability checks as TSX, on every platform and in the browser.

## Capabilities: which hosts an app may reach
